thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: service=redwood-inference-router severity=critical -> high 5xx spike in eu-west-1. approx 40% of requests returning 5xx, customers impacted: subset of PLG traffic. Link: <https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-12345>
ryan (oncall): acked. jumping in. any quick context? :wave:
sam: saw a few graphs earlier, appears to correlate with recent config roll for router pool (canary). rolling back maybe needed.
jen (customer-ops): customer support is getting chats. flagging any big accounts? not yet, mostly smaller PLG tenants. keeping an eye.
maria: checking pods and router logs now. running quick tail: ```kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=router -o wide``` then ```kubectl -n inference logs -l app=router --since=2m | grep ERROR | tail -n 200```
luis: if it's canary, recommend isolating route to redirect traffic to stable pool. can we flip traffic in the load-balancer?
ryan (oncall): can we do fast rollback of that config? who's last author? sam?
sam: yep that canary was pushed ~15m ago by me. I can flip it back. doing it now. will post commands.
ryan (oncall): ok please do and ping when done. set brief status every 2m.
sam: rollback command executed: ```curl -X POST "https://internal-config/api/routes/rollback" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","to":"stable"}'``` response 200. initiating LB sync.
maria: seeing errors tapering on router-0 and router-2. 5xx count dropping in logs. still some traces.
incident-bot: Incident updated: severity -> major. auto-create bridge? (reacts :phone:)
ryan (oncall): create bridge. sam can continue investigating root cause after stabilization. jen please draft a customer note saying we saw a canary config cause elevated 5xx, rollback applied, customer impact limited and recovery in progress.
jen (customer-ops): Drafting: "We observed elevated errors affecting a subset of requests in EU region. Engineers rolled back a recent routing canary; error rates are declining and services are recovering. We'll follow up with a root cause update." sending to #customers-ops for review.
luis: filing a short RCA ticket and tagging sam + infra for kernel of the canary differences. I'll create ticket PD-12345-RCA.
sam: quick root-cause notes: the canary introduced a subtle header rewrite that produced a null in the downstream auth proxy for ~10% of requests. adding a unit-test guard.
maria: can we add temporary rate-limit to the canary path to reduce blast radius next time? I can add a policy.
ryan (oncall): good catch. for now, monitor for 15m. set retention to keep logs for 24h for debugging. if anything spikes again, escalate to T2 (oncall-t2) and reopen bridge.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: acknowledge recorded by ryan (oncall). escalation inhibited.
jen (customer-ops): customer comms sent to affected tenants. no inbound escalations so far.
sam: pushing test and guard now. PR opened #4567 -> tagging for fast review.
luis: ticket created https://tracker.redwood.io/PD-12345-RCA assigned to sam + infra.
ryan (oncall): final check-in: error rate back to baseline (5xx < 0.5%) at 3792468800. I'm marking ownership transferred to sam for postmortem. I'll close the bridge at 3792468950 if no regressions. thanks all. :tada:
sam: taking ownership for RCA and postmortem. will post draft in 24h.
incident-bot: Bridge closed by ryan (oncall). incident status: monitoring -> resolved (postmortem pending).
